release.title: Using EBX Connectors
release.summary: Connect approved sources, choose and map the data you need, test safely, and run governed data flows from EBX.

section.item: Find an available connector and open its setup page from the Connector catalog.
Save the endpoint and the credentials or key required for your approved external source.
Choose source data and map only the fields that your EBX table needs.
Validate a connection and inspect a bounded sample before you use live business data.
Run approved data flows and review their outcome in the operational views provided by your configuration.
Connection checks now provide clearer feedback and return you to the connector workspace.
For PostgreSQL, select a table or view to start a bounded read-only query, then adjust it if needed.
Packaged setup is additive so that existing customer configuration is not replaced by an update.
This is a development preview, not a formally tagged product release.
Your administrator should validate a fresh installation and an upgrade in isolated repositories before production use.
Excel connectivity needs an approved provider. Parquet support is available only when the deployment has an approved use case.
Operational views depend on the governance and monitoring configuration available in your EBX environment.
PostgreSQL use should be validated with the credentials, permissions, and target tables approved for your environment.

release.title: Catalog navigation, sign-in safety, and connector data quality
release.summary: Fixes an error opening connectors from the catalog, a data-flow action that could unexpectedly sign you out, and cleans up connector categories and the EBX connector's logo.

section.item: Opening a connector from the Connector catalog no longer shows "The view [ConnectorView] was not found."
Opening a connector, or returning to the catalog, now stays in the perspective you opened it from instead of switching to the full administration data browser.
Editing a data flow from a connector's Data flows tab no longer risks signing you out when you close it.
Opening a data flow's visual designer ("Design/test") no longer risks signing you out when you close it either.

Connector catalog categories now reflect what each connector actually does: OpenStreetMap Nominatim, Wikidata, and the countries reference connector are grouped under Location & reference data; the French business-registry search under Corporate registries; EU customs number validation under Risk & compliance.
The "EBX (another instance)" connector now shows the real ON EBX logo instead of a placeholder image.
The JD Edwards and Oracle Fusion connectors each show their own distinct logo instead of both showing an unrelated Oracle wordmark.
A connector's resource path no longer overflows past the "Catalog branding" panel on its record form.
A couple of catalog logos (Wikidata, the Slack/Microsoft Teams webhook) were touched up for clarity.
Closing a data flow opened from a connector's own record can occasionally leave the panel loading; refreshing the page resolves it.

release.title: Lineage of every data flow, and the EBX instance in the data catalog
release.summary: Outbound runs now describe themselves to an OpenLineage sink (the ON EBX data catalog, Marquez, DataHub), and the EBX connector inventories, profiles and traces an EBX instance for the catalog like a database.

section.item: New connector type "openlineage": declare one (base URL = the sink's endpoint, its authentication) and every outbound run is described there as an OpenLineage RunEvent — the EBX table as input, the connector's object as output, one column-lineage entry per rule, the counts of the run. Inbound runs on request (emit.inbound), chat webhooks, LLM and sink connectors never described.

The EBX connector gains the data-catalog operations catalog, profile, sample and lineage: tables and columns from the Data Services metamodels, exact row counts, statistics and samples from the first records, the foreign keys of the models as column lineage. An EBX instance — this one through its own Data Services — is scanned by the catalog like any source.
Every run (REST, workflow, scheduler, user service) buffers its results per mapping and sends one event per mapping when it ends; a single call or a table trigger sends its own event.

The connector's Connection tab now says which credentials to enter for the chosen authentication: offered modes as cards, a required / optional / derived / not used state and a contextual label on each credential field, what to enter, where to get it and what is sent, and a warning when a pasted secret is longer than the field accepts.
The OpenLineage run id is derived from the Connectors run id and the mapping, so a replay updates the same run.
A newly created sink connector is seen by running synchronisations within thirty seconds; editing it re-reads it at once.

release.title: Data flows in the catalog as soon as they are declared
release.summary: A mapping no longer has to run before the data catalog shows where the data goes: it is described when it is created or changed, and retired when it is deactivated or deleted.

section.item: Every mapping is described to the OpenLineage sinks as soon as it is declared, as an OpenLineage job event carrying the same datasets and column lineage as a run: the triggers of the mapping, input and rule tables send it once the changes stop, a deactivated, deleted or renamed mapping retires its job, and every mapping is swept once at startup. The data catalog shows these flows as declared, then as observed after their first run. Sink property emit.declared (default true).

POST /ebx-connectors/rest/v1/lineage/declare and the MCP tool connectors_lineage_declare send the declared lineage of every mapping, or of one, on request — after adding a sink or changing a connector's base URL.

On a message broker (Kafka, RabbitMQ, JMS, ActiveMQ, Azure Service Bus) the lineage names the topic or queue — the mapping's input, else the connector's default topic — instead of the table label of the document, and a base URL without a scheme (host:port, bootstrap servers) gives a proper namespace.
Changing a connector's base URL does not re-describe its mappings: run lineage/declare afterwards.

release.title: A dedicated Slack connector
release.summary: Slack is reached through its Web API with the bot token of a Slack app, stored encrypted, instead of a webhook URL that carries its own secret.

section.item: New connector type "slack" and a seeded connector Slack: post (channel by id or #name, title, thread, Block Kit blocks), update (edit a posted message), dm (a member found by email), channels (search), and notify, identical to post, so a flow written for the Slack / Teams webhook moves over by changing its connector.

Workflow tasks in Slack: set the workflow trigger ChatWorkItemTrigger on a workflow model and every new work item is posted with a link that opens it in the user's EBX inbox; the message turns into "Accepted by …" or "Rejected by …" when the work item ends. The decision stays in EBX, in the user's own session. Channels per role and the public EBX address are properties of the Slack connector.

Slack refusals are errors even though Slack answers them with HTTP 200: a missing scope, an app not invited to the channel or an unknown member fails the run with the reason and what to fix, instead of counting as sent.
Slack connectors are left out of the lineage by default, like the chat webhook (exclude.types).

Connect no longer marks a valid Slack incoming webhook as failed: it is checked with an empty message that Slack refuses without posting. A Teams or Power Automate webhook, which cannot be checked without posting, stays not connected instead of failed, like any connector that offers no connection check.

release.title: Expanded connector catalog and governed metadata discovery
release.summary: The catalog now declares 92 connector types, adds governed shared-drive and SQL Server metadata discovery, and verifies packaging, catalog seeds, guides, artwork, and masking in the baseline build.

section.item: The connector catalog has expanded to 92 registered types with additive installer records and packaged implementations.
Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive can inventory explicitly scoped file metadata and source governance labels without downloading file bodies.
Microsoft SQL Server catalog scans can retain bounded source extended properties and optional usage counters with explicit retrieval status.
Administrators can request an on-demand catalog preview; only explicitly public, untagged scalar columns are shown and all other values remain masked.
The baseline now checks the release-readiness verifier, connector guide index, WAR classes, additive catalog seeds, and documented connector artwork.
The Connector catalog is now the Connection catalog, since each card is a configured connection, and its search row offers a New connection button that opens the standard creation form.
Developers and agents can isolate build output with EBX_BUILD_DIR so concurrent verification runs do not delete each other's classes.
Shared-drive pagination, metadata-only operation allowlists, SQL metadata bounds, and preview reauthorization fail closed when scope or authorization changes.
Provider-specific connectors remain under review until they pass live acceptance with approved tenant credentials, permissions, drivers, and representative non-production data.
The original guides index all 46 connector-specific guides; connector types without an individual guide remain visible in the main user guide and generated capability report.

release.title: Documents, DAMA assets and images read by an AI model
release.summary: The documents connector fills record fields from PDF, Word and text documents, from documents stored in the EBX Digital Asset Manager, and, when you allow it, from images and scanned PDFs. Uncertain values wait for a data steward.

section.item: New connector type "documents": the attributes you list are read from a document by your language-model connector, each with a confidence and the words of the document that state it. Values below the confidence threshold are proposed in the conflict manager instead of being written.

Documents stored in the EBX Digital Asset Manager (DAMA) can be read from the record that holds them, with your own permissions, so a workflow step or a table trigger can fill the record's fields from its document.
The annotate operation writes the extracted values back to the DAMA asset as metadata and adds tags chosen only from the tags DAMA already has; it never creates a tag.

Images (png, jpeg, gif, webp) and PDFs without a text layer can be sent to a model that accepts images, once you set vision=true on both the documents and the language-model connectors. Values read from an image are capped below the threshold, so a data steward confirms them by default.
Images and scans are never sent to a model unless both connectors allow it: they can contain personal data such as faces, signatures or identity numbers, and they leave EBX for the model provider.
Writing metadata and tags back to DAMA has been tested without a live DAMA instance only; validate it on a test asset first, since added metadata and tags are not removed by the connector.
Reading images has been confirmed with an OpenAI model; other providers and scanned PDFs still need a check on your environment. Azure and Ollama models take images but not PDFs.

release.title: ebx-connectors 1.4.0: change data capture, a safer entry, and three functions shipped closed
release.summary: Part 1, open: Debezium change data capture into EBX tables, deeper BigQuery, SAP OData and Workday connectors, bounded request bodies, a stricter MCP entry, and a status route that shows the outbound queue and the capture flows. Part 2, shipped as a preview and CLOSED until the server administrator opens it with -Debx.connectors.preview: documents and images read by an AI model, Match and Merge around a capture batch with golden records out, and Amazon Redshift. Read the upgrade guide (docs/UPGRADE-ROLLBACK.md, from 1.3.1 to 1.4.0) before the first start.

section.item: Debezium change data capture: operation "cdc" of a kafka connection applies a topic of Debezium events to an EBX table (insert and update as upserts, delete as delete, flag or ignore). The resume position is saved only after EBX applied the whole batch, so a failed batch is read again (at least once, replay is harmless). You see it in the run message ("CDC: 9 event(s) -> 2 upsert(s), 2 delete(s)") and in /v1/status, block cdc. To use it: docs/CDC.md. Exercised on a live Kafka broker with Debezium-format events; a real Debezium connector has not been tried yet.

BigQuery follows page tokens, polls running jobs and gains catalog, profile and sample; SAP OData fetches a fresh CSRF token and retries a rejected write once; Workday pages its REST collections and refreshes its token after a 401. Tested against recorded answers only: none of the three has been run against a real tenant. Run a read on your tenant before relying on them.
The module's services (conflict manager, synchronise, delete mapping, OpenAPI import) appear in one submenu of the Actions menu instead of side by side. Nothing to do.

GET /ebx-connectors/rest/v1/status now shows the outbound queue (waiting, retrying, set aside, age of the oldest waiting row) and each capture flow (running now, resume position, time of the last applied batch), plus preview, requestLimits and the reading of the two egress lists. Use it as the health route of a monitoring probe; the last failure of a capture flow is not in it (read it with connectors_run_get).

The two lists ebx.connectors.egress.privateExceptions and ebx.connectors.allowedHosts now say what they read: one line in the kernel log at each start (entries read, entries ignored) and a WARN when the value looks like a file path without the "file:" prefix, which used to be read silently as one entry that matches nothing. If you see that WARN, add "file:" in front of the path. The same figures are in /v1/status, block egress.

Two optional fields were added to the data model: FieldProvenance.source (where a value was read, filled by document feeds) and OutboundQueue.publish (golden, filled by a trigger that asks for golden records). Existing rows get an empty value; nothing is lost. Restart Tomcat after replacing the war so that the model is reloaded.

The war now carries Jackson 2.14.2 and the SLF4J API in WEB-INF/lib, so it can start on a standard ON EBX lib/ (ebx.jar, a database driver, jakarta.mail); before, it was dead at start there (NoClassDefFoundError on com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/JsonNode) and only worked where a FastTrack lib/ supplied them. The offline suite now fails if any class the war references is found nowhere, and the libraries that stay absent on purpose (optional features of the drivers) are listed connection by connection in the operator guide, section 1.1. tools/install.sh into a FastTrack workspace keeps that workspace's own WEB-INF/lib, so the demonstration instance keeps the Jackson of its server lib/.

Request bodies are bounded. POST /rest/mcp: 4 MiB, 20 messages per batch, nesting depth 64; the REST routes that take a document (webhook, /config, /publish, /connectors/openapi, /templates/import): 32 MiB, depth 64. A call over a bound is refused before it is parsed with 413 CN_BODY_TOO_LARGE, 400 CN_BATCH_TOO_LONG or 400 CN_JSON_TOO_DEEP and the text names the JVM property to raise (ebx.connectors.mcp.maxBodyBytes, .maxBatch, .maxJsonDepth, ebx.connectors.rest.maxBodyBytes, .maxJsonDepth). Raise one only if a legitimate caller needs it; every caller with a Connectors right can then make the server buffer that much.

An authenticated session that holds no Connectors right now gets HTTP 403 on POST /rest/mcp before its body is read (before: the call was answered and the tools were hidden or refused one by one). An MCP client configured with such an account shows a refusal at connection: give the account the READ right in the Access rights table, or stop using it.

The Google property serviceAccountFile can only name a file inside the directory of -Debx.connectors.secrets.dir (a relative name is resolved there); with no such directory it is refused. A Google connection that pointed at a key file elsewhere on the server fails at its next use with "serviceAccountFile is refused". Move the key file into the secrets directory, or use serviceAccountJson or a secret reference.

On a capture feed, a run-time input (connectors_sync inputs, a scheduled task, a workflow task) can no longer replace what the mapping configures (delete mode, flag field, topic, matching): only maxEvents and maxBytes are accepted, and only downwards. The others are dropped and named in the run message and in a WARN. An operator who used to switch "flag" to "delete" for one run must now change the mapping.
The GitHub workflow that runs the offline contracts and the dependency check was an invalid file since 2026-10-24, so neither had run on GitHub; it is readable again.

PREVIEW, CLOSED BY DEFAULT. Three functions are in the war but refuse to run until the server administrator names them in the JVM property -Debx.connectors.preview, a comma-separated list of documents, cdcMatching and redshift (exact spelling; a misspelt word opens nothing and is logged once). Closed means a run, a call, a scheduled task or a trigger send ends with an error that starts with [CN-PREVIEW-CLOSED] and names the word to add; the connection rows stay listed and editable. /v1/status, block preview, shows what is open. An instance that already uses one of them must add the word BEFORE its first start on 1.4.0.

Preview (word: documents): connection type "documents" reads PDF, Word and text documents (uploaded, or from a folder under ebx.connectors.documents.roots) and fills record fields through your language-model connector, each value with a confidence and the words of the document that state it; values under the threshold are proposed in the conflict manager. The seeded "Documents" connection is created only when the function is open, and with no language model: choose it yourself in the property llm.connector. Exercised on the test instance with a real model (36 checks).

Preview (word: documents): documents kept in the Digital Asset Manager are read from the record that holds them with the caller's own permissions, and the annotate operation writes extracted values back as DAMA metadata and tags chosen from DAMA's own vocabulary. Written back without a live DAMA instance in the tests: try it on a test asset first, the connector cannot remove what it added.

Preview (word: documents): images and PDFs without a text layer can be sent to a model that accepts images, only when vision=true is set on both the documents and the language-model connections. Values read from an image are capped at 0.7 confidence so a steward confirms them. Confirmed with an OpenAI model only.

Preview (word: cdcMatching): on a capture feed, matching=afterApply pauses Match and Merge during the batch, matches the records it created or updated and saves the resume position only when that matching ended; matching=off pauses it and matches nothing; publish=golden on an outbound trigger sends a merged record's golden record. While closed, a capture mapping that carries matching=afterApply or off is refused when saved and when run, and a queued golden send stays in the outbound queue. Not run on an instance yet (RC scenario B8).

Preview (word: redshift): connection type "redshift" on the shared JDBC engine (catalog, profile, sample, query, watermark feeds). The Amazon driver is not in the war: supply redshift-jdbc42 yourself. The cluster-identifier URL form and the options plugin_name and CredentialsProvider are refused. Never run against a real cluster.

The PDF reader of the documents function is the module's own code and has not been hardened against hostile files: a crafted PDF of under 20 kilobytes can exhaust the memory of the whole server JVM (audit C3-01, reproduced offline). This is why the function ships closed. Do not open "documents" where a user you do not trust can run a documents flow or upload to one.

Nothing in this release has been installed on an instance other than the owner's test instance, and no upgrade from 1.3.1 and no rollback has been rehearsed on a copy of a repository. docs/UPGRADE-ROLLBACK.md says which steps are read from the code and which were measured.
Nothing records what is sent to a language model; the documents function sends the document text (and, with vision on, the image) to the model you chose.

From 1.3.1: replace the war with its libraries as a unit, restart Tomcat (the model gains two optional fields, no key changes: tools/schema_diff.py reports 2 additive changes and no data-affecting change), add -Debx.connectors.preview=... first if you use documents, matching around capture, or Redshift, then run tools/smoke.sh and read /v1/status (preview, requestLimits, egress, outboundQueue, cdc). New JVM properties and their defaults: -Debx.connectors.preview (everything closed), ebx.connectors.mcp.maxBodyBytes / maxBatch / maxJsonDepth, ebx.connectors.rest.maxBodyBytes / maxJsonDepth.

release.title: ebx-connectors 1.4.1: libraries updated for published security advisories
release.summary: The war now carries Jackson 2.18.12 (11 advisories closed on 2.14.2), snappy-java 1.1.10.12 (3) and proton-j 0.35.0 (1), with no change to the functions of 1.4.0. Jackson 2.15 and later reads with limits, so the module's read limits are now written down and shown in the status route. The installation script now puts these libraries into the FastTrack workspace, and the package refuses a library that has an unaccepted advisory. Read the upgrade guide (docs/UPGRADE-ROLLBACK.md, from 1.4.0 to 1.4.1).

section.item: Jackson 2.14.2 became 2.18.12 (jackson-core, jackson-databind, jackson-annotations, jackson-datatype-jsr310): 11 published advisories (OSV, read on 2026-11-12), among them parsing of deeply nested documents and of very large numbers, are closed. snappy-java 1.1.10.5 became 1.1.10.12 (3 advisories, used by Kafka compression) and proton-j 0.34.1 became 0.35.0 (1 advisory, used by the Azure Service Bus client). OSV reports no advisory against the new versions at the date of the package. Two advisories stay accepted on purpose, as before: the RabbitMQ client (amqp-client 5.35.0) and the H2 driver (2.1.212); runtime-libs/DEPS-KNOWN.txt gives the reason of each.

tools/package.sh now asks OSV about every library of the war (73 of 73; seven were never asked before because their Maven group or version could not be read) and refuses the package on an advisory that DEPS-KNOWN.txt does not accept, with its reason, or when OSV cannot be reached. The only way past an unreachable OSV is the named variable CONN_PACKAGE_OSV_WAIVER, whose text is written into the package (RELEASE-NOTES.md and DEPENDENCY-CHECK.txt). The ordinary offline test suite is unchanged: it never uses the network.

Jackson 2.15 and later refuses a JSON document nested deeper than 1000 levels, a number of more than 1000 characters, a name of more than 50,000 characters and a string of more than 20,000,000 characters. The module keeps the first three as they are and sets the last one on purpose: a document sent in base64 inside a JSON string can be larger than 20 million characters on the REST routes (32 MiB by default), and the answers of called services are read up to 128 MiB, so the string limit now follows those byte limits (the larger of them: 134,217,728 characters by default) and the byte limits stay the ones that govern. -Debx.connectors.json.maxStringLength=N sets it explicitly. What the module's reader really carries, and the Jackson version, are in GET /ebx-connectors/rest/v1/status, requestLimits.jackson. The depth the module accepts from a caller stays 64 and is refused before any parsing (400 CN_JSON_TOO_DEEP); a number, a name or a string refused by Jackson inside a body that passed the byte limit is answered as a parse error (400, JSON-RPC -32700), never as a server error. The answer of a called service nested deeper than 1000 levels is not parsed into a tree (the raw text is kept), as an unparsable answer already was.

tools/install.sh (installation into a FastTrack workspace) now puts the libraries of runtime-libs/ into the workspace's WEB-INF/lib: it adds a missing one, replaces another version of the same library, leaves every jar it does not know (such as ebx-connectors-extension-sample.jar), and prints the three lists; --dry-run shows them without writing. Before, it kept that folder as it was, so the demonstration instance would have run the new code on the old Jackson.

The OpenAPI import in YAML no longer depends on a Jackson YAML library in the Tomcat lib/ folder: the war carries jackson-dataformat-yaml 2.18.12 and SnakeYAML 2.3. A YAML factory taken from a server lib/ that holds Jackson 2.14 could not be used by the module's Jackson 2.18 (two class loaders). A YAML specification larger than 3 MiB is now refused with a clear message (SnakeYAML's own limit); JSON has no such limit.

The new libraries were tested offline only (the suite, a Service Bus message built and encoded by the Azure client, a snappy round trip, a Jackson read-limit test with the module's real entries). This package has not been installed on a running instance, and no Kafka, Azure Service Bus or REST call has been made with it. Run tools/smoke.sh and one read per connection type you use after the upgrade.
Jackson 2.15 and later reads some documents differently from 2.14: see docs/UPGRADE-ROLLBACK.md, section from 1.4.0 to 1.4.1, for what was looked at and what was not.

From 1.4.0: replace the war with its libraries as a unit and restart Tomcat; the data model is unchanged (no schema change, no new field). On a FastTrack workspace, install with tools/install.sh (its output lists the libraries it replaced). Check GET /ebx-connectors/rest/v1/status: version 1.4.1, requestLimits.jackson.version 2.18.12 and readersCarryTheSetting true. New JVM property: ebx.connectors.json.maxStringLength (optional). Rolling back to 1.4.0 is the previous war with its previous libraries.
